caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001074
attempts.paper_title: Kalugin PN, et al. Simultaneous, real-time tracking of many neuromodulatory signals with multiplexed optical recording of sensors on a micro-endoscope. Neuron (2026).
attempts.entry_title: In vitro calibration of MORSE probes (Kalugin et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Only the in vitro calibration of the ten-sensor probes could be tested, and most of it did not reproduce. Cell numbers per gel and sub-minute onset times held, the latter marginally, and sensor yield was partly met (559 labelled cells against 506). Table 1 EC50s and peak responses, EC50 consistency across probes, and the AVP-OXT crosstalk did not reproduce, likely because the sensor labels and the authors' hand corrections are not in the data. The slice, in vivo CSF, probe stability, ELISA and choroid plexus findings could not be tested for lack of labels, event times or raw data.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kalugin et al. (2026) on dandiset 001074, which holds the CaImAn traces and masks of the paper's MORSE recordings without sensor labels or stimulus timing. With the well order of the paper's code, it labels the cells of the ten ten-sensor revision probes and tests sensor yield, crosstalk, EC50s, peak responses and onset kinetics, and it tests the cell counts per gel and the cells tracked across recordings. The slice and in vivo claims cannot be tested on the deposited files.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kalugin et al. (2026) from dandiset 001074

outcomes.notes: Recordings are matched by date and probe in the subject names (for example sub-251003-PL65-wells001). All ten identification recordings have 1023 frames (11 wells of 93) and all ten dose recordings 1395 (15 wells). 86% of 829 cells rise most steeply within the first minute of a well, against 23%, 11% and 3% with the onsets shifted by 15, 31 and 46 frames. In the dose recording, 79% of the 559 labelled cells rise more in the block of their own mixture; per sensor 0.73 to 0.92, except the DA sensor cells (41%), which also respond to the NE of the other block. Label check (added in revision): under both labelling readings the plateau of every sensor's mean identification trace rises most in its own ligand's well (10 of 10; 0.47 to 0.74 of the peak-normalized range in reading b). This is not independent of the labels, which are made from the time of each cell's steepest rise.
deviations: The link claim and its criterion were written by the author during the analysis, after the frame counts were seen; its thresholds (more than half) are the author's.

outcomes.notes: Reading (b), curated masks per recording (mr-raw files), over 59 recordings of 43 probes after removing duplicates. Masks per recording range from 21 to 205 (median 128; given as measured), and 38 of 43 probes (0.88) have a mean count in 90 to 220. With the further merged mr-m-raw masks, 31 of 38 probes. In each of the five revision identification recordings with an mr-raw file, mask centres fall in the top (5 to 21 cells), middle (44 to 88) and bottom (27 to 67) thirds of the imaged z range, and so do the matched masks of the dose recordings of all ten revision probes (top 3 to 21, middle 18 to 79, bottom 3 to 66). The volumes read have 17 to 24 planes against the 30 of the Methods. Reading (a), CNMF components before curation, is not in the dandiset and was not tested.
deviations: Reading (a) of the criterion cannot be run; only reading (b) is tested.
Assumed that the gel thickness is the imaged z range of each recording (16 to 26 planes); the claims file and the paper do not say how the thickness is bounded.
Depth uses the masks reordered from their scrambled storage (see findings).
Probes are pooled over all contexts (dipping, slice and in vivo recordings); Figure 1C shows one dipping probe.

outcomes.notes: Reading (b), pooled clustering plus a per-probe pass, gives 559 labelled cells (expected 455 to 557), median 9 sensors per probe, 25th percentile 8, 75th 9, and 6.82 cells per sensor per probe (expected 5.42 to 6.62). Reading (a), pooled only, gives 384 cells, median 8.5, 8 and 9, and 4.74. Sensors per probe are 5, 8, 9, 10, 5, 9, 10, 9, 8, 9 against the code's 5, 8, 9, 10, 6, 9, 10, 9, 9, 9. Variants (b and a): the code's 30-frame window 550 and 383 cells (6.71 and 4.73); without the peak rule 606 and 402 (7.21 and 4.90); a whole-well boxcar 539 and 372 (6.57 and 4.59). The sensor counts match; the cell counts do not under any variant. The run of the first round gave 382 cells in reading (a); this run gives 384, with the same code. The claims file's header gives the derivative window as 30 frames, the Methods 1 minute (31 frames); this is asked of a reader in questions/001074.yaml.
deviations: The dandiset gives no sensor labels. Labels are made from the identification traces by the Methods' procedure (Quantification and statistical analysis, paragraphs 2-3) with these choices, assumed where the Methods do not fix them. The jump artefact is an exponential with the Methods' 30 s decay scaled by the jump measured as in morse_figs3_rev cell 23. The exponential background is fitted only when two wells precede activation, with its decay bounded by the fitted segment. The ligand administration time course used to match clusters is a boxcar over the first minute of each well (a whole-well boxcar is shown as a variant), and a match is kept only when the cluster's mean derivative also peaks in that ligand's well. This peak rule is the author's own, not in the Methods; it leaves 47 cells unlabelled in reading (b) and 18 in reading (a), and results without it are shown.
The code's hand corrections of clusters (morse_figs3_rev cells 73-78) are not repeated, so the labelled cells are not the paper's 506.
The time base is the code's 31 frames per minute (93 per well); the files state 30 Hz.

outcomes.notes: All ten sensors carry labels, on 5 to 10 probes each. As the criterion is written, the mean peak-normalized trace is highest in the sensor's own or partner's well for 2 of 10 sensors by the per-well maximum (OXT, ATP) and 3 of 10 by the per-well mean (adding ACh), under both labelling readings. Allowing the well after the ligand's, as the code does for AVP, NE and CCK (cell 248), 7 of 10. For CCK and MT the maximum is in the PBS well, for NE, DA and ACh in the ATP well. Responses persist into later wells; measured as the rise of each well's plateau over the previous well's, every sensor rises most in its own ligand's well (10 of 10, both readings). Whether Figure 1G means the highest level or the onset is asked of a reader in questions/001074.yaml; the outcome follows the criterion as written. Changed from partially_reproduced after the verifier's round 1.
deviations: Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b).
The criterion's background correction is the one of fig1g-sensor-yield.
Variant added in revision, the largest rise of the well plateau (mean of the third minute) of the mean trace over the previous well's plateau, the first well over the mean of its first 10 frames.

outcomes.notes: With the Methods' 1-minute window and the reading (b) labels, DA-NE has the largest correlation (0.77); AVP-OXT is 0.16, rank 12 of 45, below 5-HT-DA (0.46), DA-ACh (0.45), 5-HT-NE (0.37) and NE-ACh (0.33). With the code's 10 frames, DA-NE 0.83 and AVP-OXT 0.43, rank 14. With the reading (a) labels, DA-NE 0.63 and 0.70, AVP-OXT rank 15 and 16. The DA-NE crosstalk holds; the AVP-OXT part and the "only" do not, since 10 to 14 other pairs lie above AVP-OXT. Changed from partially_reproduced after the verifier's round 1, as two of the criterion's three conditions fail.
deviations: Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b); reading (a) shown.
The band-pass artefact variant of morse_figs3_rev cell 219 was not run.

outcomes.notes: Reading (i), the code's baseline and peak wells with the Methods' third-minute mean, puts 2 of 10 EC50s within 10% (OXT 2217 nM, CCK 266 nM; given as measured, in nM). Reading (ii), the code's plateau, 0 of 10; reading (iii), Eq. 28 over the recording after an exponential background, 0 of 10, with 3 of its 14 fits on the 1 pM lower bound, since Eq. 9 has no offset; variant (iii-b), the lowest-well plateau subtracted first, 0 of 10; reading (iv), reading (i) on the cells kept by the code's noise cut, 2 of 10 (5-HT 632 nM, DA 1622 nM). The median absolute log10 ratio to Table 1 is 0.37, 0.30, 1.48, 0.29 and 0.12. With the reading (a) labels, 2, 1, 0, 1 and 3 of 10 (median ratio 0.11 to 0.67). The median normalized plateaus rise from 0 to about 1 over each group's wells, but single cells reach -35 to 161, and the pooled least-squares fits follow them.
deviations: Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b); the paper's cells differ. Reading (a) shown.

The Methods do not say how the dose recording is background corrected and normalized. Reading (i) follows the code (baseline-well subtraction and peak-well normalization, morse_figs3_rev cells 338-339, 365) and is taken as the main reading, an assumption; the others are shown.
The code's per-cell background fits over hand-set windows (cells 285-293) cannot be repeated, and its pooling with an older probe set for ACh, ATP, MT and HA is not run.
Concentrations of the mixture wells, 10 to the power (k - offset) M, are from morse_figs3_rev cell 345.

outcomes.notes: Reading (i), in nM (given as measured); reading (iv) gives 558, 20.2, 2957 and 4379 nM. None of the four is within 10% under any of the five normalizations or either labelling reading. The off-target groups are normalized to their own peak well in the partner's block (the code's groups 1, 2, 7 and 8); since F is free in the fit, this does not change the EC50.
deviations: As table1-ec50-on-target.

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), the ligand's well, puts 4 of 14 within 10% (AVP, 5-HT, ACh, HA); reading (b), the code's wells, 5 of 14 (adding NE 0.338). Of the values outside tolerance in reading (a), NE (0.303) and the OXT sensor to AVP (0.044) are below the paper's and the other eight above, up to MT 0.564 against 0.30. The medians are over the cells with a positive peak (13 to 89 per group). With the reading (a) labels, 2 of 14 in either well, every on-target median above Table 1 (MT 0.827). Changed from partially_reproduced after the verifier's round 1: the criterion asks each value within 10%, and 9 or more of 14 are not.
deviations: Labels and corrections as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b); reading (a) shown.

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), every per-probe EC50 within a tenth to ten times the consensus, holds for 2 of 10 sensors (ACh, HA); against the Table 1 EC50 instead of the consensus, 3 of 10; reading (b), SEM below half the mean, for 6 of 10. On the cells kept by the noise cut, 7 and 8 of 10. With the reading (a) labels, 6, 6 and 8 of 10. Neither reading holds for all sensors in any variant, so the criterion (both must hold) is not met. Per-probe EC50s span orders of magnitude for some sensors (DA 69 nM to 1.05 mM).
deviations: As table1-ec50-on-target; probes with more than one cell of the sensor (3 to 9 per sensor).

outcomes.notes: Median tau-on under 60 s for 10 of 10 sensors on the normalized dF/F0 (28.6 to 53.7 s) and 8 of 10 on the Eq. 8 concentration (34.4 to 58.9 s for those; AVP 74.2 s and 5-HT 62.3 s). Both readings meet at least 8 of 10, so the outcome is the one both give. The outcome rests on the labelling: with the reading (a) labels the concentration fits give 7 of 10 (MT 63.6 s), so the two readings of the criterion would differ there. With the EC50s fitted in reading (i) of table1-ec50-on-target in place of Table 1's, 8 and 7 of 10 (reading b labels), 10 and 8 (reading a). Fixing xinf to the median of frames 47-78, as the code does, underestimates long time constants (a synthetic 40-frame tau is fitted as 24.7); with xinf fitted, 9 and 6 (b) and 8 and 6 (a). The outcome is marginal: the concentration count is exactly at the threshold (8 of 10), and each alternative (the reading (a) labels, the fitted EC50s, xinf fitted) gives a split between the criterion's two readings, so it holds only under the main choices. The "most signals plateau within 1 minute" part of the statement is not tested by the criterion.
deviations: The well and the concentration conversion use the claims file's CONSTANTS (Table 1 EC50s, the code's F), since the EC50s fitted here do not reproduce Table 1.
Labels as in fig1g-sensor-yield, reading (b), assumed; reading (a) shown. Dose traces normalized as in reading (i) of table1-ec50-on-target.
tau is fitted by least squares over a grid and a bounded search; the code uses curve_fit.

outcomes.notes: Slopes of concentration tau-on against depth are positive for 5 of 10 sensors (AVP, 5-HT, NE, MT, HA) and negative for OXT, CCK, DA, ACh and ATP, in the code's orientation; the opposite orientation gives 5 of 10 as well. With the reading (a) labels, 7 of 10 positive (OXT, CCK and ATP negative), 3 of 10 in the opposite orientation. No variant reaches 9 of 10. The largest slope is 0.52 s per um, so the slopes are modest as read. Correlations are weak (MT r = 0.56 and 0.51, the others at most 0.24 in size).
deviations: Depth is the z centre of mass of each reordered mask in the dose recording, relative to the probe's shallowest cell, at 9.89 um per plane; the orientation (depth growing as the plane index falls) is taken from morse_figs3_rev cell 718 and assumed to hold for the deposited plane order.
tau-on as in figs3e-tau-on-under-one-minute.

outcomes.notes: In the code's Figure S2F sets (morse_figs2_2 cell 2; ten dipping probes with 40 pairs, 22 in vivo recordings matched to their post hoc dipping, 11 slice pairs of which two are not in the dandiset), per-probe mean matched counts range from 27 to 108 (given as measured), and 26 of 39 probes (0.67) lie in 63 to 143: 8 of 10 dipping, 15 of 22 in vivo and 3 of 7 slice probes. Of the 71 pairs of these sets with a matched file, 70 have both the reference's and the moving recording's matched<k> file (20230922-PL28 pair 3 has only the reference's), and in 69 of the 70 the two hold the same count (20230922-PL28 pair 0 does not); the 70 include 29 dipping pairs with k of 1 or more, all equal. Over all 72 probes of the dandiset and 110 pairs, 44 (0.61) are in range (15 of 21 dipping, 24 of 40 in vivo, 5 of 11 slice), means 10 to 140, with 2 to 8 recordings per probe. The slice probes alone are not mostly in range. The claims file cites printed counts of 53 to 108 in morse_figs2_2 cell 4; that cell has no outputs at the pinned commit.
deviations: The probe sets are those of morse_figs2_2 cell 2, listed in the notebook; the figure's in vivo n=25 and slice n=15 are not the code's 22 and 11, and two of the code's slice probes (20230509-DA1PL53, 20230607-SL1PL47) are not in the dandiset. All probes of the dandiset are shown as a variant.

Assumed that a matched<k> file holds the k-th pair of a probe; the files do not say. The reading is taken from the code (8_mask_matching cell 8 writes one pair's matched masks to both recordings; morse_figs2_2 cell 3 loads matched{k} for the k-th pair). Duplicated files are counted once; for 20230922-PL28 the pairs are taken from wells001, whose matched suffixes are consistent (the matching notebook, cells 15-17, re-saves that probe's matched1 file as matched).

outcomes.notes: Needs the demons deformation fields or the raw imaging. The dandiset holds CaImAn traces and masks only; the paper says raw imaging is available from the authors on request.
Needs deformation fields or raw imaging of the 33 test probes; not in the dandiset, and no file names the hydrogel recipe or KOH treatment.
Needs deformation fields or raw imaging, and a record of which probes were unstable. The dandiset holds only the recordings that were processed; the files give no stability flag.
Needs the raw GRAB and tdTomato imaging and the Cellpose probability maps; neither is in the dandiset.
Needs all 48 slice probes with deformation fields or imaging; the dandiset holds 22 slice recordings (86 files) of CaImAn output only.

The slice files give no brain region (dLGN, PVH or LC), no KCl or ligand wash-on times and no sensor labels. The slice probes' post hoc dipping files (wells001) exist for some, but their well order is not in the files. The paper's code (morse_fig2_rev) holds hand-picked windows for the LC slices only, and the code that made the dLGN and PVH numbers is not in the repository (claims file header).

The LC analysis was not attempted with the code's hand-set frames in the time available.

The in vivo files (mouse) give no IP or ICV injection times, no injected ligand order (which varies by mouse, morse_fig3_rev cell 0) and no sensor labels; the post hoc dipping files exist for some mice but name no wells.
The fiber photometry recordings are not in the dandiset (the paper says they are available on request).

Needs sensor labels for the four ten-sensor in vivo probes (morse_fig3_rev cells 162, 204: 231105-DG39PL32, 231107-DG44PL58 and two 2025 probes). The two 2023 probes' post hoc dipping recordings have 3588 frames, 23 wells at the 52 frames per minute the code uses for them; their well order is in neither the files nor the code, and the code loads their cluster labels from files outside its repository (cell 170). The two 2025 probes (ZS93ZS22-251121, ZS94ZS19-251122) have 1023-frame dipping recordings with the revision probes' 11-well order (cells 51-56); labelled as those are, in the notebook, they carry 7 and 6 sensors (reading b; 6 and 6 in reading a) and 7.15 cells per sensor per probe, against the code's 9, 8, 9 and 5 sensors for its four probes. The median and mean over four probes cannot be computed from two.

findings.statement: No file gives the sensor expressed by each cell, though the identities were made by post hoc dipping and every analysis of the paper rests on them. No file gives well, wash-on, KCl, optogenetic or injection times, the ligand of each well, the brain region of a slice or the injections of a mouse; there is no acquisition or stimulus data. Only the in vitro dipping of the ten revision probes could be labelled, from the paper's code.

Every file states an imaging rate of 30 Hz and timestamps from 0 in steps of 1/30 s, the same session start (2023-01-01T12:30), the indicator OGB-1 and the location "brain". The Methods give about 0.5 volumes per second (31 per minute in the code for the 2025 recordings, 52 per minute for some 2023 ones), the sensors are GRAB sensors, and the dipping recordings are of HEK cells in a hydrogel, not of a mouse brain. The session dates are only in the subject names.

The 3D image masks are stored scrambled. Each is the Fortran-order flattening of the (x, y, z) volume written into a C-order array of the same shape, so read as stored every mask spans the full width of the volume with equal weight in every plane; reordered with order="F" it is a compact cell.
67 files belong to a subject named "0" with session names that carry no context. 16 of them repeat named files of 20230922-PL28, 20230829-SL1PL56 and 220408-PK27PL20; the other 51 cannot be placed.
The six files of sub-250918-SL1ZS5-slice and of sub-250918-SL1ZS5-wells001 are identical in shape and values, so one recording of that probe is deposited under both names and the other is missing.

The matched-file suffixes of probe 20230922-PL28 do not fit its pairs. wells201 holds a "matched" and a "matched1" file that are copies, and the "matched" file of wells401 has 96 cells, the count of wells001's "matched3", where wells001's "matched" has 82.

The matched pair of probe 251119-ZS16 has 143 cells in wells001 and 142 in wells101; the paper's code deletes row 53 of the identification file (morse_figs3_rev cell 6), which nothing in the files records.

The accepted and rejected columns of every PlaneSegmentation are all false, so they carry no curation information, and the stage of each file (mr-raw, mr-m-raw, refit, matched<k>) is described only by the paper's code README.
The mask volumes have 16 to 26 planes, where the Methods describe 30 planes per volume (about 270 um); the files do not say whether planes were cropped.

The deformation fields, raw two-photon imaging, Cellpose probability maps, fiber photometry, ELISA and mass spectrometry tables, choroid plexus imaging and histology are not deposited. The paper states that raw imaging and photometry are available on request; 13 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

Questions for the authors. (1) Sensor identity. The Methods' clustering without the code's hand corrections (morse_figs3_rev cells 73-78) gives 384 or 559 labelled cells against 506 (382 in the first run); which corrections were made and why? (2) Dose-response normalization. The Methods say "corrected with an exponentially decaying background fit and then peak-normalized"; the code subtracts a baseline well and divides by a peak well, after per-cell background fits over hand-set windows (cells 285-293, 338-339). Which windows and wells were used, and is the noise cut of cells 343 and 365 part of the published fits? The EC50s fitted here depend strongly on this (median log10 distance from Table 1 0.12 to 1.48 across the normalizations with the reading (b) labels, 0.11 to 0.67 with the reading (a) labels). (3) Is the deposited plane index the code's z, so that depth from the front face grows as the index falls (cell 718)? (4) How was the jump artefact's 30 s decay and the background-fit window chosen per recording?

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive listing for blocked claims and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs; it did not re-run cells. It agreed with 44 of 47 outcomes.

disagreements.reason: All 10 labels are present, but the mean trace is highest in its own or its partner's well for only 2 of 10 sensors by the per-well maximum and 3 of 10 by the mean; even allowing the next well, CCK, NE and DA fail. The per-well maximum favours later wells when responses do not wash out, so the failure may come from carry-over; DA peaking in the ATP well suggests poor DA labels (B3). Reading (a) is not carried in (B2).
NE-DA is the largest correlation (0.77), but AVP-OXT ranks 12th of 45 (14th with the 10-frame variant); 5HT-DA, DA-ACh and 5HT-NE all lie above it. Reading (a) is not carried in (B2).
4 of 14 (well reading a) and 5 of 14 (code's well, reading b) within 10%. MT is 0.56 against 0.30; CCK 0.49 against 0.40.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 47 outcomes. It also quoted cell 6, "All dipping files but a few have frame counts that are multiples of 93", where cell 5 prints 254 of 384 (130 files, 34%, are not); the sentence now gives these counts. Of its round-1 points it listed B8 (the residual of the jump removal) and the 13/14 in vivo stability denominator as not acted on and not affecting a conclusion. B8 is left as is, since the jump is measured as the code measures it (morse_figs3_rev cell 23); the stability denominator cannot be tested, since the files give no stability flag and hold only processed recordings, as the notes of methods-revision-probe-stability say.
